abez.title: Abez
abez.note: A border town of Issachar, somewhere in the Jezreel Valley. It appears once, in the list of that tribe's towns, and its site has never been identified.

abiezer-2.title: Abiezer
abiezer-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
abiezer-2.note: The man Gideon's clan is named after, in Manasseh. Gideon's own description of that clan, when he was called, was the weakest in the tribe.

achor.title: Achor
achor.note: A valley near Jericho, on the border between Judah and Benjamin, named for the trouble Achan brought on Israel.

achsah.title: Achsah
achsah.note: Caleb's daughter, married to Othniel after he took a Canaanite city. She asked her father for springs of water, and got them.

achshaph.title: Achshaph
achshaph.note: A Canaanite royal city whose king went into the northern coalition that Joshua broke at the Waters of Merom.

achzib.title: Achzib
achzib.note: A town given to Judah, in the lowland lists. Micah puns on the name when he gets to it.

achzib-2.title: Achzib
achzib-2.note: The other Achzib, a Phoenician town on the coast inside Asher's territory that Israel never fully took.

adadah.title: Adadah
adadah.note: Far south in Judah, out in the Negev. Nobody has identified the site.

adamah.title: Adamah
adamah.note: A fortified town of Naphtali, probably the modern Damiyeh on the west side of the Sea of Galilee, though that identification is not certain.

adami.title: Adami
adami.note: A point on Naphtali's boundary in lower Galilee, written more fully as Adami-nekeb, and where exactly it stood has not been established.

adithaim.title: Adithaim
adithaim.note: A lowland town of Judah, named once between Sharaim and Gederah, and its site is still unidentified.

adullam.title: Adullam
adullam.note: A Canaanite royal city in the Shephelah, near the valley of Elah. David killed Goliath in that valley. Later, running from Saul, he hid in a cave near Adullam, and his family joined him there, and so did everyone in distress.

adummim.title: Adummim
adummim.note: The name means the red ones, and it was a pass on the road between Jerusalem and Jericho. It marked the boundary between Judah and Benjamin.

ahiman.title: Ahiman
ahiman.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ahiman.note: One of the descendants of Anak. That clan's size terrified the Israelite spies. Decades later Caleb drove Ahiman and his brothers out of Hebron, the land he had been promised.

ai.title: Ai
ai.note: A fortified Canaanite city near Bethel. Israel's first attack was thrown back because of Achan's hidden sin, and once that was dealt with Joshua took the city by ambush. The site is usually identified with et-Tell, though digging there has turned up little from the right period.

aijalon.title: Aijalon
aijalon.note: In the valley of Aijalon Joshua told the moon to stand still alongside the sun during the battle against the Amorite coalition. Later it marked the boundary of Danite and Benjamite territory.

ain.title: Ain
ain.note: Given to Simeon inside Judah's territory, and later made one of the cities handed to the Levites.

alammelech.title: Alammelech
alammelech.note: The name means king's oak. It sat inside Asher's border, between Achshaph and Amad, and its site is unidentified.

amad.title: Amad
amad.note: Named once, between Alammelech and Misheal on Asher's border, and its site has not been identified.

amam.title: Amam
amam.note: One verse of Joshua's town lists puts it in the Negev district of Judah with Shema and Moladah. That is all that survives of it, and nobody knows where it stood.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

anab.title: Anab
anab.note: Joshua drove the Anakim out of this town in the Judean hill country. It still has its old name, in the ruin Khirbet Anab southwest of Hebron.

anaharath.title: Anaharath
anaharath.note: A border town of Issachar, listed with Shihon and Rabbith, tentatively placed near Mount Tabor in the Jezreel Valley.

anakim.title: Anakim
anakim.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
anakim.note: A people of unusual height living in Canaan before the conquest. Ten of the twelve spies came back afraid of them, and that fear is why Israel spent forty years in the wilderness.

anim.title: Anim
anim.note: In Judah's hill country near Eshtemoa, south of Hebron, and commonly identified with the ruin of el-Ghuwein.

aphek.title: Aphek
aphek.note: The Philistines captured the ark of the covenant from Israel at Aphek. A later battle there went the other way, when Israel beat the Arameans after Elisha promised King Jehoash the victory.

aphek-2.title: Aphek
aphek-2.note: Two battles happened here. The Philistines took the ark from Israel at Aphek, and later Israel beat the Arameans here, exactly as Elisha had said.

aphekah.title: Aphekah
aphekah.note: A town in Judah's hill country, not one of the several places called Aphek even though the names share a root. Its site is unknown.

arab.title: Arab
arab.note: A town near Hebron in Judah's hill country, likely home to Paarai the Arbite of David's mighty warriors. It is generally identified with the ruin of er-Rabiyeh, south of Hebron.

arad.title: Arad
arad.note: Its king attacked Israel as they came up toward Canaan from the south and took prisoners, and Israel destroyed the town under the ban. The Canaanite city lay about 20 miles south of Hebron, at Tel Arad.

archi.title: Archi
archi.note: Hushai's clan. He was the loyal friend of David who worked against Ahithophel's advice during Absalom's rebellion.

arnon.title: Arnon
arnon.note: A swift river running into the Dead Sea from the east, the line between Amorite and later Moabite land and Israel's tribes beyond the Jordan. Its gorge still carries water in the Wadi al-Mujib. King Mesha of Moab's inscription, the Moabite Stone, boasts of building a highway across it.

aroer.title: Aroer
aroer.note: A border town on the edge of Moabite and Ammonite territory. It marked the southern limit of the land Israel took east of the Jordan.

aroer-2.title: Aroer
aroer-2.note: A second town of the name, in Numbers 32:34 and Joshua 13:25, on the same border between Israel's lands east of the Jordan and Ammonite territory.

ashan.title: Ashan
ashan.note: A small town in Judah's lowlands, later handed to Simeon, whose share lay inside Judah. Aaron's line of Levites got it as a priestly city. Nobody has found the site.

ashdod.title: Ashdod
ashdod.note: Ashdod spelled another way, one of the five chief Philistine cities, on the coast between Ekron and Gaza. The captured ark was put in its temple of Dagon, and the affliction started there.

ashdoth-pisgah.title: Ashdoth-pisgah
ashdoth-pisgah.note: The slopes of Pisgah, east of the Jordan, in land taken from Sihon the Amorite. It is likely a description of the ridge rather than a place name, the same ridge Moses looked at the promised land from before he died.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

ashnah.title: Ashnah
ashnah.note: Two towns in Judah's lowland share the name. One sat near Zorah and Eshtaol, the other near Nezib and Keilah, and neither site is certain today.

ashriel.title: Ashriel
ashriel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ashriel.note: Asriel, from Manasseh. His family made one of the tribe's clans.

ashtaroth.title: Ashtaroth
ashtaroth.note: Ashtaroth under another spelling, the fortified capital of Og, king of Bashan, east of the Jordan. It went to the half-tribe of Manasseh and then to the Levites of Gershon. The name comes from the goddess Ashtoreth, and the site is generally put at Tell Ashtarah in the Golan.

ataroth.title: Ataroth
ataroth.note: Named twice, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

ataroth-addar.title: Ataroth-addar
ataroth-addar.note: A town on the line between Ephraim and Benjamin, in Joshua's boundary lists twice, and no confident modern identification has been made.

avim.title: Avim
avim.note: A town in Benjamin's territory, and not the Avvites of the coast near Gaza. Its site is unknown.

avims.title: Avims
avims.note: The Avvim lived in villages around Gaza before the Caphtorim, from Crete, drove them out. 2 Kings 17:31 gives the same name to settlers from Avva placed in Samaria by the Assyrians.

azekah.title: Azekah
azekah.note: A fortified town in Judah's Shephelah. Joshua routed five Amorite kings near it in a hailstorm. A Lachish ostracon written during Nebuchadnezzar's last campaign says the writer is watching for Lachish's signal fires but cannot see Azekah, which some read as Azekah already fallen and others as a line of sight he never had.

azem.title: Azem
azem.note: Also Ezem, a town in the far south of Judah later given to Simeon. Its site in the Negev has not been identified with confidence.

aznoth-tabor.title: Aznoth-tabor
aznoth-tabor.note: The summits of Tabor, or the ears of Tabor, one of the marks on Naphtali's boundary near Mount Tabor. It may have been a cluster of hills rather than a town.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

baal-gad.title: Baal-gad
baal-gad.note: The farthest north Joshua's conquests reached: a Canaanite town in the valley under Mount Hermon, named for the Baal worshipped there. It lay near the sources of the Jordan.

baalah-2.title: Baalah
baalah-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

baalah.title: Baalah
baalah.note: Another name for Kiriath-jearim, the town that kept the ark of the covenant for twenty years until David took it to Jerusalem. A second Baalah, near Beersheba, turns up later in the same chapter of Joshua.

baalath-2.title: Baalath
baalath-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

baalath-beer.title: Baalath-beer
baalath-beer.note: Baalah of the well, a town of Simeon's on the southern edge of Judah's land, probably the one the parallel list calls just Baal.

balaam.title: Balaam
balaam.about: Prophet living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
balaam.note: A prophet, but not an Israelite. Balak of Moab hired him to curse the Israelites. On the way his donkey saw an angel blocking the road that Balaam himself missed, and God made the animal speak to rebuke him.

balah.title: Balah
balah.note: Bilhah in 1 Chronicles 4:29, Baalah in Joshua 15:29, Balah here: three spellings of one town of Simeon's inside Judah's territory.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

bealoth.title: Bealoth
bealoth.note: Down in the far south of Judah, likely the same town as Baalath-beer. Solomon's list of districts also names a region Aloth or Bealoth under one of his twelve governors.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

beeroth.title: Beeroth
beeroth.note: It was one of four Hivite cities, with Gibeon, Chephirah and Kiriath-jearim. Their people tricked Joshua into a peace treaty by dressing up as travellers from far away. Later it was allotted to Benjamin.

bene-barak.title: Bene-barak
bene-barak.note: A town allotted to Dan in the coastal plain. It is identified with modern Bnei Brak near Tel Aviv-Jaffa, and the name is still in use.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

beor.title: Beor
beor.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
beor.note: Balaam's father, named whenever Balaam is called son of Beor.

beten.title: Beten
beten.note: A town on Asher's border. Nobody has placed it with confidence.

beth-anath.title: Beth-anath
beth-anath.note: House of Anath, named for the Canaanite goddess. Naphtali was given this fortified town. They never drove out the Canaanites in it and put them to forced labor instead.

beth-anoth.title: Beth-anoth
beth-anoth.note: A hill-country town of Judah, generally identified with the village of Beit Ainun northeast of Hebron.

beth-arabah.title: Beth-arabah
beth-arabah.note: House of the desert plain, a small town in the Jordan Valley near the Dead Sea. It sat on the line between Judah and Benjamin, and Joshua 15:61 counts it among Judah's wilderness towns.

beth-aram.title: Beth-aram
beth-aram.note: It belonged to Gad, east of the Jordan and opposite Jericho, probably the Beth-haran of Numbers 32:36. Herod Antipas later rebuilt it and renamed it Livias after the Roman empress.

beth-aven.title: Beth-aven
beth-aven.note: House of vanity. It lay in the hill country of Benjamin near Ai and Bethel, served as a boundary marker in Joshua, and was where Israel's forces gathered before Jonathan's fight with the Philistines in 1 Samuel 14.

beth-baal-meon.title: Beth-baal-meon
beth-baal-meon.note: East of the Jordan, on the tableland Reuben was given. The text uses several forms of the name, Baal-meon and Beon among them. Later the town passed into Moabite hands.

beth-dagon.title: Beth-dagon
beth-dagon.note: House of Dagon. This one was in the lowland plain of Judah near Philistine country, identified with Beit Dajan near Lydda. Another town of the same name stood elsewhere.

beth-dagon-2.title: Beth-dagon
beth-dagon-2.note: House of Dagon, and two towns carry it. This one sits on Asher's border.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-emek.title: Beth-emek
beth-emek.note: A border town of Asher, near the ravine of Jiphthah-el. Its site is unidentified.

beth-hoglah.title: Beth-hoglah
beth-hoglah.note: House of the partridge, a town on the line between Judah and Benjamin near the Jordan and the Dead Sea. It is usually identified with Ain Hajlah, a spring a few miles southeast of Jericho.

beth-horon.title: Beth-horon
beth-horon.note: Twin towns on the pass from the coastal plain up into the hill country. Joshua's army came this way chasing the Canaanite coalition in the battle where the sun stood still.

beth-horon-2.title: Beth-horon
beth-horon-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

beth-jeshimoth.title: Beth-jeshimoth
beth-jeshimoth.note: Israel's camp on the plains of Moab, the last before they crossed the Jordan into the promised land.

beth-lebaoth.title: Beth-lebaoth
beth-lebaoth.note: In the Negev, a town of Simeon's inside Judah. Joshua 15:32 has it as Lebaoth and 1 Chronicles 4:31 as Beth-birei, three spellings taken to be one town.

beth-nimrah.title: Beth-Nimrah
beth-nimrah.note: Gad rebuilt this fortified town east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho, after asking for the well-watered land of Gilead for their livestock.

beth-palet.title: Beth-palet
beth-palet.note: House of flight, a town in the far south of Judah, in the district bordering Edom. It turns up again after the exile, spelled Beth-phelet.

beth-pazzez.title: Beth-pazzez
beth-pazzez.note: A town of Issachar, listed beside En-haddah in Joshua 19:21. Nothing else is recorded about it, and its site is unidentified.

beth-shean.title: Beth-shean
beth-shean.note: After Saul died on Gilboa, the Philistines hung his body and his sons' bodies on the walls of this city. Beth-shean was Canaanite, in Manasseh's land. It stood where the Jezreel and Jordan valleys meet.

beth-shemesh.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh.note: It was a Levitical city on Judah's northern border, its name meaning house of the sun. When the Philistines sent the ark back, it came here first and was welcomed with sacrifice.

beth-shemesh-2.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh-2.note: Named twice, in Joshua and Judges, and nowhere else.

beth-shemesh-3.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh-3.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

beth-tappuah.title: Beth-tappuah
beth-tappuah.note: House of apples, a hill-country town of Judah. It survives as the Palestinian village of Taffuh, about five miles west of Hebron.

beth-zur.title: Beth-zur
beth-zur.note: A fortified town in the hill country of Judah, a few miles north of Hebron. Rehoboam strengthened it as part of the defences of his kingdom once the ten northern tribes had broken away.

bethlehem-2.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

bethmarcaboth.title: Bethmarcaboth
bethmarcaboth.note: House of the chariots, a town of Simeon's in the far south of Judah. Where Joshua 15:31 lists Judah's towns, Madmannah stands in its place.

bethpeor.title: Bethpeor
bethpeor.note: Across the Jordan from Jericho, in Reuben's land. The sanctuary of Baal-peor nearby gave it its name. Moses gave his final address to Israel in the valley there.

bethuel-2.title: Bethuel
bethuel-2.note: It was a town in the south, in Simeon's land, called Bethul in Joshua 19:4 and Bethel in 1 Samuel 30:27. It is not the famous Bethel near Jerusalem, and it has no tie to the Aramean Bethuel.

betonim.title: Betonim
betonim.note: On the northern edge of Gad's land east of the Jordan. Its exact site is unknown.

bezer.title: Bezer
bezer.note: A city of refuge for Reuben, east of the Jordan. Anyone who killed a person by accident could run there for protection. It was one of three such cities on that side of the river.

bizjothjah.title: Bizjothjah
bizjothjah.note: In the Negev, near Beersheba, one of the towns given to Judah.

bohan.title: Bohan
bohan.note: A Reubenite. The stone of Bohan, named after him, marked part of the border between Judah and Benjamin.

bozcath.title: Bozcath
bozcath.note: A town in the Shephelah of Judah near Lachish and Eglon. Adaiah came from there. His daughter Jedidah was the mother of King Josiah.

cabbon.title: Cabbon
cabbon.note: A lowland town of Judah in the district that held Lachish and Eglon. It is not mentioned anywhere else and remains unidentified.

cabul-2.title: Cabul
cabul-2.note: A town on the eastern border of Asher. Another Cabul, a district of twenty towns in Galilee, got the name later.

caleb.title: Caleb
caleb.about: Joshua's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
caleb.note: One of the twelve spies Moses sent into Canaan. He and Joshua were the only two who came back telling Israel to trust God and take the land, and the rest of that generation paid for ignoring them with forty years in the wilderness.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

carmel.title: Carmel
carmel.note: Elijah's contest with the prophets of Baal happened on this mountain ridge on Israel's Mediterranean coast. Fire came down from heaven when Elijah prayed, and Baal had nothing to answer with.

chefarhaamonai.title: Chefarhaamonai
chefarhaamonai.note: The villages of the Ammonites, a town allotted to Benjamin. It is listed beside Ophni and Geba, never mentioned again, and its site is unknown.

chephirah.title: Chephirah
chephirah.note: With Gibeon, Beeroth and Kiriath-jearim, one of the four Hivite towns whose people tricked Joshua into a peace treaty by posing as travellers from a far country.

chesalon.title: Chesalon
chesalon.note: On Judah's northern border, on the slope of Mount Jearim. It is identified with the village of Kesla in the hill country west of Jerusalem.

chesil.title: Chesil
chesil.note: A Negev town of Judah, likely the place Joshua 19:4 calls Bethul and 1 Chronicles 4:30 calls Bethuel.

chesulloth-2.title: Chesulloth
chesulloth-2.note: Issachar's town on the slopes between Jezreel and Shunem. It is usually taken to be the same place as Chisloth-tabor on Zebulun's boundary, at modern Iksal near Mount Tabor, which would put the two tribal lines meeting at one town.

chinnereth.title: Chinnereth
chinnereth.note: Before anyone called it Gennesaret or Tiberias, the lake was the Sea of Chinnereth, named for a fortified Canaanite city on its northwest shore. The town fell inside Naphtali's land. Under the plural Chinneroth it named the whole district, which Ben-hadad of Syria raided in Baasha's reign.

chisloth-tabor.title: Chisloth-tabor
chisloth-tabor.note: The name means the loins of Tabor, a point on Zebulun's boundary near the mountain. Usually placed at the village of Iksal, about two and a half miles west of Tabor, and it may be the town called Chesulloth a few verses on.

dabareh.title: Dabareh
dabareh.note: Also called Daberath, on Zebulun's border near Mount Tabor, and later given to the Gershonite Levites. The Arab village of Deburiyeh at the western foot of Tabor still carries the name.

dabbesheth.title: Dabbesheth
dabbesheth.note: One of the towns marking Zebulun's border; nothing else is recorded and the site has not been found.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

dannah.title: Dannah
dannah.note: One of the towns in Judah's hill country south of Hebron. It is sometimes put near modern Idhna, southwest of Hebron, but that is not certain.

debir.title: Debir
debir.note: Othniel took this town in Judah's hill country and won Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife for it. Debir is also the name of a Canaanite king Joshua defeated.

dibon.title: Dibon
dibon.note: A Moabite city Israel took and rebuilt. King Mesha names it on the Moabite Stone as one of his own building projects.

dilean.title: Dilean
dilean.note: A town in the Shephelah of Judah, listed with Migdal-gad and Mizpeh, whose site has not been identified with confidence.

dimonah.title: Dimonah
dimonah.note: A town in the far south of Judah, in the Negev, generally taken as the Dibon resettled after the exile in Nehemiah 11:25.

dor.title: Dor
dor.note: A royal Canaanite port on the coast south of Mount Carmel. Joshua beat its king, but its people were never fully driven out, and it later went into one of Solomon's districts. Excavation at Tel Dor traces the shift from Canaanite to Phoenician on that coast.

edar-2.title: Edar
edar-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

edrei.title: Edrei
edrei.note: Israel met Og, king of Bashan, here, and his whole kingdom fell in that one battle.

eglon.title: Eglon
eglon.note: A royal Canaanite city in the Shephelah. Its king joined the five Amorite kings Joshua crushed at Gibeon, and the city was destroyed and given to Judah.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

ekron.title: Ekron
ekron.note: Northernmost of the five Philistine cities, given to Judah and then Dan but never firmly held. The ark's last stop before the Philistines sent it back. Ahaziah of Israel sent there to ask Baal-zebub about his health, and an inscription at Tel Miqne naming Ikausu, or Achish, son of Padi settles the site.

ekronite.title: Ekronite
ekronite.note: Somebody from Ekron. When the ark arrived after the plagues at Ashdod and Gath, the Ekronites cried out in terror and demanded it go back to Israel.

eleazar.title: Eleazar
eleazar.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
eleazar.note: Aaron's third son. Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire, and Eleazar became high priest after his father. He worked with Moses on the second census and with Joshua on dividing the land, and his line held the high priesthood for most of the history after.

elon-4.title: Elon
elon-4.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

eltekeh.title: Eltekeh
eltekeh.note: A town given to Dan and then set aside as a Levitical city for Kohath's descendants. Sennacherib's own annals say he beat an Egyptian and Ethiopian relief army near Eltekeh in 701 BC, on the same campaign in which he shut Hezekiah up in Jerusalem.

eltekon.title: Eltekon
eltekon.note: One of eleven towns in Judah's hill country, listed with Halhul, Beth-zur and Gedor. Its site has not been found and nothing else is recorded about it.

eltolad.title: Eltolad
eltolad.note: Judah got it first and then passed it to Simeon, since Judah had more land than it needed. It is Tolad in Chronicles, still held by Simeonite families. Somewhere in the southern Negev, but the site is not settled.

en-dor.title: En-dor
en-dor.note: Home of the medium Saul went to in disguise the night before his last battle. It lay in Issachar's land, near where Deborah and Barak beat Sisera. Endur, southeast of Mount Tabor, keeps the name.

en-gannim.title: En-gannim
en-gannim.note: Fountain of gardens. This one sat on Issachar's border and went to the Gershonite Levites, and it is generally identified with Jenin, which still has the name and its springs.

en-gannim-2.title: En-gannim
en-gannim-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

en-gedi.title: En-gedi
en-gedi.note: An oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, fed by a spring that drops some 600 feet down the cliffs. David hid in its caves from Saul and spared Saul's life there. A Chalcolithic temple on the site is far older than Israel in Canaan.

en-haddah.title: En-haddah
en-haddah.note: A town on Issachar's border, next to Engannim in the list, with no site found.

en-hazor.title: En-hazor
en-hazor.note: A fortified town of Naphtali, not the big city of Hazor, named once with its site lost.

en-rogel.title: En-rogel
en-rogel.note: A spring just south of Jerusalem where the Kidron and Hinnom valleys meet. Jonathan and Ahimaaz waited there to carry news to David in Absalom's revolt, and Adonijah held his feast there to make himself king. Many put it at Bir Ayyub, Job's Well.

en-tappuah.title: En-tappuah
en-tappuah.note: The spring by Tappuah that marked the line between Ephraim and Manasseh. The town went to Ephraim though it stood on Manasseh's land.

enshemesh.title: Enshemesh
enshemesh.note: A spring on the road down toward Jericho, not far from Bethany, marking the line between Judah and Benjamin. The name means fountain of the sun, and a spring still flows on that route.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

ephron.title: Ephron
ephron.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephron.note: The Hittite who sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It was the first piece of the promised land Abraham owned, and Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and their wives were all buried there.

eshean.title: Eshean
eshean.note: A town in Judah's hill country whose site is not secure, though some put it near Dumah, south of Hebron.

eshkalonites.title: Eshkalonites
eshkalonites.note: The people of Ashkelon, one of the five Philistine cities still unconquered when Joshua was old. Digs on the coast there have found a large Philistine cemetery, which gave archaeologists the Philistines' own bones.

eshtaol.title: Eshtaol
eshtaol.note: Samson grew up here, and here the Spirit of the Lord first began to stir him. It was a Shephelah town that went to Dan, and the Danites sent their spies north from it. Samson was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in his father's tomb.

eshtemoa.title: Eshtemoa
eshtemoa.note: David sent some of the Amalekite plunder to the elders of Eshtemoa, a priestly town south of Hebron, for standing by him in his outlaw years. It survives as es-Samu, where old ruins have been found.

ether.title: Ether
ether.note: A lowland town of Judah, near Lachish in the list, later counted among Simeon's towns. The site has not been identified with confidence.

evi.title: Evi
evi.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
evi.note: One of five Midianite kings killed in the war against Midian that followed Baal-peor. His land is recalled in Joshua among what was later allotted. Nothing more is known of him.

gaba.title: Gaba
gaba.note: Another English spelling of Geba, a Levitical city in Benjamin by the pass of Michmash. Jonathan raided a Philistine garrison there, and later it marked the line between the northern and southern kingdoms.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

galilee.title: Galilee
galilee.note: Jesus grew up here and did most of his public work around the Sea of Galilee. Judeans thought the north provincial and mixed, which is the edge on Nathanael's question about whether anything good could come out of Nazareth.

gath.title: Gath
gath.note: Goliath's hometown, one of the five Philistine cities. The captured ark brought disaster on it, David later hid there with King Achish while running from Saul, and in the end David took it. Most identify it with Tell es-Safi, where a potsherd turned up carrying two names related to Goliath.

gath-kephr.title: Gath-kephr
gath-kephr.note: Jonah was born here, in Zebulun's territory, though the town is better known as Gath-hepher. Local tradition puts his tomb in the village of Mashhad by a hill called Nebi Yunus, near Nazareth.

gath-rimmon-d.title: Gath-rimmon
gath-rimmon-d.note: In Dan's territory, and given to the Kohathite Levites. A second Gath-rimmon shows up in the Manasseh list, but 1 Chronicles 6:70 has Bileam there instead, which looks like a copying slip rather than two towns with one name.

gazathite.title: Gazathite
gazathite.note: A man of Gaza. Judges uses it for the men who waited at the gate to kill Samson, and he carried the gate off.

gazer.title: Gazer
gazer.note: The same city as Gezer. Pharaoh took it and gave it to his daughter when she married Solomon, and Solomon fortified it along with Hazor and Megiddo. The Gezer Calendar, a little tablet of farming seasons in early Hebrew script, was found there.

geder.title: Geder
geder.note: Joshua beat its king. Whether it is the same place as Gedor or Gederah is possible, not certain.

gederah.title: Gederah
gederah.note: It sat in the Shephelah, Judah's lowland, and Chronicles names potters of Judah's line who lived there and worked for the king.

gederoth.title: Gederoth
gederoth.note: The Philistines took it in the reign of Ahaz, while Judah was worn down by war with Israel and Syria. It was a Shephelah town, and the name means sheepfolds.

gederothaim.title: Gederothaim
gederothaim.note: Listed right after Gederah in Joshua 15:36. The ending can mean two, so some read it as the two Gederahs rather than a town of its own, and if it was separate nobody has found where.

gedor.title: Gedor
gedor.note: A town in the hill country of Judah between Jerusalem and Hebron, whose founders Chronicles traces through Hur and Ephrathah. The same name belongs to another place and to a man in Saul's family.

geliloth.title: Geliloth
geliloth.note: On Benjamin's border, near the Jordan. It is generally taken as another name for the Gilgal of Joshua 15:7, though which Gilgal is uncertain, since the name just means circles.

geshur.title: Geshur
geshur.note: It was a small Aramean kingdom northeast of Galilee, and Absalom ran there after murdering his brother Amnon and stayed three years under his grandfather the king.

geshuri.title: Geshuri
geshuri.note: David married Maacah, daughter of Talmai, the king of Geshur, and so these people were Absalom's family on his mother's side. Their small Aramean kingdom lay east of the Sea of Galilee.

gibbethon.title: Gibbethon
gibbethon.note: In Dan's territory and assigned to the Kohath family, but the Philistines held it most of the time. Nadab was besieging it when his officer Baasha killed him and took the throne. A generation later Elah went the same way while his army was at the same city again.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gilead-2.title: Gilead
gilead-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
gilead-2.note: The man, not the region. Numbers 26 and Joshua 17 put him in Manasseh's family, and Chronicles lists him there again.

gilgal.title: Gilgal
gilgal.note: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan. The people were circumcised there and kept their first Passover in the land, and later Samuel judged at Gilgal and Saul was confirmed as king there.

giloh.title: Giloh
giloh.note: Ahithophel came from Giloh, in Judah's hill country southwest of Hebron. When Absalom took Hushai's advice over his, he went home to Giloh and hanged himself.

gittite.title: Gittite
gittite.note: A man from Gath. Obed-edom the Gittite kept the ark in his house before David brought it up to Jerusalem, and Ittai the Gittite brought his foreign troops to David's side when Absalom rebelled.

golan.title: Golan
golan.note: One of the three cities of refuge east of the Jordan, in Bashan, where someone who had killed by accident could run from revenge. It went to the Gershonite Levites and later gave its name to the region, which is why there are Golan Heights today. The exact site is not known.

goshen-2.title: Goshen
goshen-2.note: Not the Goshen in Egypt but a stretch of Canaan's south that Joshua took, along with a town of the same name in the hill country.

hadashah.title: Hadashah
hadashah.note: A lowland town of Judah, in the district with Lachish. The name means new, and it is never mentioned again.

halak.title: Halak
halak.note: The bare mountain rising toward Seir, the southern edge of what Joshua took. Several barren ridges south of the Dead Sea have been suggested and none is certain.

halhul.title: Halhul
halhul.note: Joshua 15:58 lists it in Judah's hill country, and it still goes by almost the same name, Halhul, a Palestinian town just north of Hebron.

hali.title: Hali
hali.note: On Asher's border, between Helkath and Beten in the lists.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hammath-2.title: Hammath
hammath-2.note: Its name means hot springs, and it was a fortified town of Naphtali on the Sea of Galilee. The thermal baths just south of Tiberias are the site, where a synagogue with a zodiac mosaic floor has been dug up.

hammon.title: Hammon
hammon.note: Two towns. One was in Asher near Sidon, probably Umm el-Amoud, and the other a Levitical city in Naphtali, likely Hammath by the Sea of Galilee.

hannathon.title: Hannathon
hannathon.note: It lay on Zebulun's border in Galilee, and the Amarna letters of the fourteenth century BC already name it, as Hinnatuna, a garrison town fought over on the road through Galilee.

haphraim.title: Haphraim
haphraim.note: Issachar's town near Shunem in Joshua 19:19. El-Afuleh in the Jezreel Valley is the tentative match, on geography more than evidence.

hazar-gaddah.title: Hazar-gaddah
hazar-gaddah.note: One of the towns in the far south of Judah's allotment, near the border with Edom, and its site has not been found.

hazar-shual.title: Hazar-shual
hazar-shual.note: Village of the jackal. It sat on Judah's southern border and later fell inside Simeon's share, and people came back to live there after the exile. It is commonly placed near Tell es-Sa'weh, between Beersheba and Moladah.

hazar-susah.title: Hazar-susah
hazar-susah.note: Village of the horse, a town on Judah's southern border that went to Simeon.

hazor.title: Hazor
hazor.note: The head of all the Canaanite kingdoms, in Joshua's words, and the biggest city-state in the region. Its fall decided the northern campaign. The dig there found a huge Bronze Age city to match.

hazor-3.title: Hazor
hazor-3.note: It is new Hazor, Hazor-hadattah, in the far south near Moladah, and Joshua 15:25 is its only appearance.

hazor-4.title: Hazor
hazor-4.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

hazor-5.title: Hazor
hazor-5.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

hebron-4.title: Hebron
hebron-4.note: A border town of Asher, sometimes spelled Ebron, and not the Hebron of Judah. Some manuscripts read Abdon here, and where it was is uncertain.

helek.title: Helek
helek.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
helek.note: From Manasseh through Gilead, he headed the Helekite clan, counted in the census and given land.

heleph.title: Heleph
heleph.note: Naphtali's boundary starts here. The name means exchange. Nobody has found the place.

helkath.title: Helkath
helkath.note: Asher's town, given with its pastures to the Gershonite Levites. Chronicles calls it Hukok.

hepher-2.title: Hepher
hepher-2.note: Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Kings, and nowhere else.

hepher.title: Hepher
hepher.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hepher.note: Gilead's son, of Manasseh, and the father of Zelophehad. Zelophehad had five daughters and no son, and their case before Moses won daughters the right to inherit.

hermon.title: Hermon
hermon.note: On Israel's northern border, and the snowmelt off it gives the Psalms their picture of dew. It is near Caesarea Philippi, which makes it a likely site for Jesus's transfiguration.

heshbon.title: Heshbon
heshbon.note: Sihon's capital, east of the Jordan near the northern edge of Moab. Moses took it before Israel crossed into Canaan, and it became a Levitical city in Reuben. Moab later had it back, which is why the prophets name it in their judgments on Moab, and the ruins, still called Hesban, lie about twenty miles east of the Jordan.

heshmon.title: Heshmon
heshmon.note: One of the southernmost towns given to Judah in the Negev, toward the border of Edom, and nobody has found where it was.

hezron.title: Hezron
hezron.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hezron.note: Perez's son, and the line that ends in David runs through him; Ruth closes with it and Matthew picks it up. The same name marks a spot on Judah's southern border, west of Kadesh-barnea.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

hoglah.title: Hoglah
hoglah.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hoglah.note: One of Zelophehad's five daughters. They asked Moses for their father's land, got it, and set a precedent for Israel.

holon.title: Holon
holon.note: In the hill country of Judah, and later one of the towns given to the Levites.

horem.title: Horem
horem.note: A fortified town of Naphtali, listed with Iron and Migdal-el. The name means roughly "sacred place", and the site is unknown.

hormah.title: Hormah
hormah.note: Its name means "devoted to destruction", and it was first called Zephath. Israel was beaten there after going into Canaan without the Lord, following the spies' report. Later Israel vowed to destroy the cities of the region, and the vow, kept under Joshua, gave the town its name.

hosah-2.title: Hosah
hosah-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

humtah.title: Humtah
humtah.note: A hill-country town of Judah, grouped with Hebron in Joshua's list, and its site has not been found.

hur-2.title: Hur
hur-2.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hur-2.note: Numbers and Joshua name him twice, and he is a king from the wilderness years.

ibleam.title: Ibleam
ibleam.note: A town given to Manasseh inside Issachar's borders, where the Canaanites were never driven out. King Ahaziah of Judah took his death wound near there, running from Jehu. It is generally identified with Khirbet Bel'ameh, near Jenin.

idalah.title: Idalah
idalah.note: On Zebulun's border, listed with Shimron and the Bethlehem of Zebulun. It is often placed near the Kishon valley, though nobody is sure.

iim.title: Iim
iim.note: The name means ruins, and two places carry it. One is a town in the far south of Judah near Edom; the other is a late stop in the wilderness, just before Israel reached Moab's border.

iron.title: Iron
iron.note: In Upper Galilee, a fortified town of Naphtali, and nothing to do with the metal. It is generally identified with the modern village of Yarun, which keeps the old name.

irpeel.title: Irpeel
irpeel.note: One of Benjamin's fourteen cities near Gibeon, and no trace of it has been found.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

ithnan.title: Ithnan
ithnan.note: Far south in Judah near Edom, listed with Kedesh and Hazor, and no trace of it has been found.

ittahkazin.title: Ittahkazin
ittahkazin.note: A marker on Zebulun's border, found in Joshua 19:13 and nowhere else. Nobody has located it.

jaazer.title: Jaazer
jaazer.note: Jazer, an Amorite town in Gilead east of the Jordan. Israel took it and gave it to Gad, then to the Levites of Merari. Isaiah and Jeremiah both use its ruined vineyards as a picture of Moab's ruin.

jabbok.title: Jabbok
jabbok.note: Jacob crossed this stream alone the night before he met Esau, wrestled until daybreak, and came away named Israel and limping. It runs west into the Jordan through a gorge in Gilead, halfway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, and is the Zarqa River today.

jabin-2.title: Jabin
jabin-2.note: Joshua names him once, and he is a king from the years before the monarchy.

jabneel.title: Jabneel
jabneel.note: On Judah's northwestern border near the coast, the town later called Jabneh or Jamnia. Uzziah tore down its walls.

jabneel-2.title: Jabneel
jabneel-2.note: Two towns carry the name, not a man, and this one is on Naphtali's border.

jagur.title: Jagur
jagur.note: On Judah's southern border, toward the edge of the Negev, and the site has not been found.

jair-5.title: Jair
jair-5.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

janoah-2.title: Janoah
janoah-2.note: On Ephraim's northeastern border, in the Jordan Valley. It is identified with the village of Yanun, southeast of Nablus.

janum.title: Janum
janum.note: A hill-country town of Judah near Hebron, listed with Beth-tappuah and Aphekah and never mentioned again.

japha.title: Japha
japha.note: The Hebrew name for Joppa, the port that is Jaffa today. Solomon's cedar came in by sea there, and so did Ezra's timber for the second temple, and Jonah sailed from it toward Tarshish. The Amarna letters already mention its guarded gate.

japhia-3.title: Japhia
japhia-3.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

japhleti.title: Japhleti
japhleti.note: A border mark in Joshua 16:3, "the border of the Japhletite", on the edge of Ephraim's land. The clan is otherwise unknown and was probably Canaanite.

jarmuth.title: Jarmuth
jarmuth.note: Its king joined the march on Gibeon after Gibeon made peace with Israel, and Joshua beat them in the battle where the sun stood still.

jattir.title: Jattir
jattir.note: A priests' town in the hill country of Judah, given to Aaron's line. David sent its elders a share of the Amalekite plunder, as he did for many towns while he was on the run. It is identified with Khirbet Attir, south of Hebron.

jearim.title: Jearim
jearim.note: A wooded ridge on Judah's northern border. The name means "forests", and it lives on in Kirjath-jearim, "city of forests", the town nearby.

jehoshua.title: Jehoshua
jehoshua.about: Judge living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
jehoshua.note: Joshua, in the longer spelling. Moses's attendant and successor, and one of two from the generation out of Egypt who lived to enter the land. He took Israel over the Jordan, brought down Jericho and divided the land among the tribes. The name means Yahweh saves, the same name Greek renders Jesus.

jehud.title: Jehud
jehud.note: A town of Dan on the coastal plain, between Baalath and Bene-berak. It survives as Yehud, near Lod.

jephthah.title: Jephthah
jephthah.note: Son of a prostitute, thrown out by his half-brothers, and leading a gang of raiders when Gilead's elders came begging him to fight the Ammonites. He vowed to sacrifice whatever came out of his house first after the victory, and it was his daughter, his only child. Judges tells it without approving the vow or explaining why he kept it.

jephunneh.title: Jephunneh
jephunneh.about: Caleb's father living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jephunneh.note: Caleb's father, remembered almost entirely as a name in "Caleb son of Jephunneh", which is how the Old Testament tells that Caleb apart from the others.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jethlah.title: Jethlah
jethlah.note: A town on the border of Dan's land, listed with Aijalon and Timnah in Joshua 19:42, its exact location unknown.

jezreel.title: Jezreel
jezreel.note: A valley and town in northern Israel. Naboth's vineyard was there, the one Ahab and Jezebel stole, and it was there that Jehu wiped out Ahab's whole house. Hosea named one of his children Jezreel to say judgment was coming.

jezreel-2.title: Jezreel
jezreel-2.note: Not the northern valley. This Jezreel is a town in the hill country near Hebron, listed in Joshua 15:56.

jobab-5.title: Jobab
jobab-5.note: One of 5 men called Jobab. This one is a king from the years before the monarchy, named once in Joshua.

jokdeam.title: Jokdeam
jokdeam.note: In the hill country of Judah, listed near Maon and Carmel. Its site is unidentified.

jokneam.title: Jokneam
jokneam.note: Joshua defeated its king. It sat near Mount Carmel by the Kishon River, inside Zebulun's land, and was later given with its pastures to the Merarite Levites. It is generally identified with Tel Yokneam, about twelve miles southwest of Nazareth.

joktheel.title: Joktheel
joktheel.note: "Subdued by God." It names a town in Judah near Lachish, and it is also what Amaziah, king of Judah, renamed Sela after he conquered Edom and slaughtered its army.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

juttah.title: Juttah
juttah.note: A hill-country town of Judah given to Aaron's line. It survives as the village of Yatta, a few miles south of Hebron, and an old tradition makes it John the Baptist's birthplace.

kabzeel.title: Kabzeel
kabzeel.note: The far south of Judah's land, out by the border with Edom. Benaiah came from there, one of David's best-known warriors and later head of his bodyguard. After the exile it seems to have been lived in again as Jekabzeel.

kadesh-2.title: Kadesh
kadesh-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

kadeshbarnea.title: Kadeshbarnea
kadeshbarnea.note: An oasis in the wilderness of Zin, on Canaan's southern edge, where Israel camped for much of the wandering years. The spies went out from here, and the people's fear at their report got that whole generation sentenced to die in the desert. Later it marked the southern boundary of the land.

kanah.title: Kanah
kanah.note: The name means reedy, and this one is a stream on the border between Ephraim and Manasseh, running from the hill country to the Mediterranean. Another Kanah, a town up in Asher, is a separate place.

kanah-2.title: Kanah
kanah-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

karkaa.title: Karkaa
karkaa.note: On Judah's southern boundary, between Adar and Azmon in the wilderness of Zin. Its exact site is unknown.

kattath.title: Kattath
kattath.note: It was a town allotted to Zebulun. It may be Kitron, one of the places where Zebulun never drove out the Canaanites, though nobody is sure of the site.

kedemoth.title: Kedemoth
kedemoth.note: A town in Reuben's land, given to the Merarite Levites. Moses sent messengers from its wilderness to Sihon, king of the Amorites, asking to pass through, and Sihon's refusal led to war.

kedesh.title: Kedesh
kedesh.note: A city of refuge in Galilee, one of six where someone who had killed by accident could run and be safe. Barak came from there, the commander Deborah called up.

keilah.title: Keilah
keilah.note: David saved this walled town from a Philistine raid while Saul was hunting him. Then he learned they would have handed him over if Saul came, and he moved on into the wilderness of Ziph.

kenaz-2.title: Kenaz
kenaz-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kenaz-2.note: Caleb's younger brother, and father of Othniel, Israel's first judge.

kenezite.title: Kenezite
kenezite.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kenezite.note: Caleb, one of the two spies who stayed faithful, is called a Kenizzite. The clan came from Kenaz and was tied to Edom in Genesis, then folded into Judah.

kerioth-2.title: Kerioth
kerioth-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

keziz.title: Keziz
keziz.note: Emek-keziz in full Hebrew, a town in Benjamin's eastern district by the Jordan valley, listed with Jericho and Beth-hoglah. No one knows exactly where it was.

kinah.title: Kinah
kinah.note: Far south in Judah, near the border with Edom, in the dry country below Beersheba.

kiriathaim.title: Kiriathaim
kiriathaim.note: It started out as a town of Reuben's and ended up in Moab, on Jeremiah's list of the cities God's judgment would fall on.

kirjath.title: Kirjath
kirjath.note: Kirjath-jearim, also called Baalah, a Gibeonite town on the line between Judah and Benjamin. The ark sat there twenty years after the Philistines gave it back, until David brought it up to Jerusalem. The prophet Uriah, whom Jehoiakim had killed, came from there.

kirjath-arba.title: Kirjath-arba
kirjath-arba.note: "Arba's city," Hebron's older name, after a great man among the Anakim. Sarah died there and Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah close by to bury her. Joshua gave it to Caleb for the faithful report he brought back as a spy.

kirjath-sannah.title: Kirjath-sannah
kirjath-sannah.note: Another name for Debir, also called Kirjath-sepher, a royal Canaanite city in the hills southwest of Hebron. Caleb promised his daughter Achsah to whoever took it, and his nephew Othniel did.

kirjathbaal.title: Kirjathbaal
kirjathbaal.note: They also called Kirjath-jearim by this name, and Baalah, a boundary town between Judah and Benjamin and one of the Gibeonite towns. The ark stayed there about twenty years before David brought it up to Jerusalem.

kishion.title: Kishion
kishion.note: A town in Issachar given to the Gershonite Levites, spelled Kishon in the second list, its exact site unknown.

kithlish.title: Kithlish
kithlish.note: In the Judean lowlands, listed with Lahmam and Gederoth. It has traditionally been placed near Jelameh, though the identification is not firmly established.

lachish.title: Lachish
lachish.note: A heavily fortified Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands. Joshua took it, Rehoboam rebuilt it into one of Judah's strongest fortresses, and in 701 BC Sennacherib's Assyrians took it again. Assyria carved the siege on wall reliefs now in the British Museum. The ruins at Tell ed-Duweir also gave up the Lachish Letters, written during Babylon's last siege, just before Jerusalem fell.

lahmam.title: Lahmam
lahmam.note: Listed with Kithlish and Gederoth in the lowland district of Judah, at a site nobody has identified.

lakum.title: Lakum
lakum.note: On Naphtali's border, listed with Adami and Jabneel, and never mentioned again.

lasharon.title: Lasharon
lasharon.note: "Belonging to Sharon." Joshua beat a king of Lasharon, but most of these verses are about the Sharon plain, the rich coast between Joppa and Mount Carmel, with royal pasture and some of Gad living there. Its beauty became a byword, "the rose of Sharon," and Isaiah pictures it blooming again.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

lebaoth.title: Lebaoth
lebaoth.note: "Lionesses." One of Judah's southernmost towns, by the Edom border, and probably the same as Beth-lebaoth, which went to Simeon.

leshem.title: Leshem
leshem.note: An older form of Laish, the Canaanite city Dan took and renamed after leaving its assigned land on the coast. Tel Dan, the site, produced the Tel Dan Stele, where an Aramean king boasts of beating the "house of David," the earliest mention of David's dynasty outside the Bible.

libnah.title: Libnah
libnah.note: A royal Canaanite city near Lachish that Joshua took and gave to the Levites in Judah. It held out against Sennacherib's Assyrians. Hamutal, Josiah's wife and mother of two of Judah's last kings, came from there.

lo-debar.title: Lo-debar
lo-debar.note: A town where, in 2 Samuel 9, a lame son of the old royal house is found living in another man's home. Amos plays on its name, which sounds like "nothing."

maachah-2.title: Maachah
maachah-2.note: A small Aramean kingdom near Geshur, east of the Sea of Galilee. Israel never managed to drive it out.

maachathite.title: Maachathite
maachathite.note: Someone from Maacah, the small Aramean kingdom near Mount Hermon that Israel never fully brought under. Eliphelet, one of David's officers, was a Maachathite.

maarath.title: Maarath
maarath.note: Hill-country Judah, near Hebron. It is often placed near Beit Ummar, a few miles north of Hebron, though the identification is not certain.

machir.title: Machir
machir.about: Manasseh's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
machir.note: Manasseh's son. His clan, the Machirites, were such fighters that Machir's name can stand for the whole half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan.

madmannah-2.title: Madmannah
madmannah-2.note: Down in the Negev, in Judah's south, and later held by Caleb's descendants. One proposed site is southwest of Gaza and another northeast of Beersheba, and neither is certain.

madon.title: Madon
madon.note: Its king joined Jabin of Hazor's coalition against Joshua at the Waters of Merom and was killed. It has been tentatively placed at a ruin near Hattin, west of Tiberias.

mahanaim.title: Mahanaim
mahanaim.note: "Two camps." Jacob met the angels of God here near the Jabbok River on his way home, and split his household in two before facing Esau. After Saul died, Ishbosheth ruled the northern tribes from Mahanaim while David held Hebron, and years later David fled there himself from Absalom and heard there that his son was dead.

mahlah.title: Mahlah
mahlah.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
mahlah.note: Zelophehad had five daughters and no son, and Mahlah was one of them; their plea to Moses to inherit his land changed the law.

makkedah.title: Makkedah
makkedah.note: Five Amorite kings ran from the battle at Gibeon and hid in a cave near this royal city in the Shephelah. Joshua sealed them in until the fighting was over, then brought them out, killed them, and hung their bodies on trees. Then he took the city.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

maon.title: Maon
maon.note: About seven miles south of Hebron, in the Judean hill country. David hid from Saul in the wilderness named after it, and Nabal, whose widow Abigail married David, kept his flocks there. The ruins, now Tell Ma'in, still mark the spot.

maralah.title: Maralah
maralah.note: A point on the southern edge of Zebulun's land, placed at Ma'lul, a village southwest of Nazareth.

mareshah.title: Mareshah
mareshah.note: Rehoboam fortified this Shephelah city, and Asa beat Zerah the Cushite's far larger army there. Micah mourns it among Judah's towns. Its ruins at Tell Sandahanna hold a Hellenistic underground city and painted Sidonian tombs full of exotic animals.

me-jarkon.title: Me-jarkon
me-jarkon.note: "Waters of yellowness," a river on the border of Dan, named next to Rakkon just before Joshua says Dan's land was too small and the tribe went north to take Laish. It is usually taken as the Yarkon, which still runs across the coastal plain near Tel Aviv from springs at ancient Aphek.

medeba.title: Medeba
medeba.note: An old Moabite town given to Reuben. Joab beat the Ammonites and their Aramean allies near it in David's time, and Moab later took it back, which Isaiah mourns in his oracle against Moab. Today it is Madaba in Jordan, known for a sixth-century Byzantine floor mosaic that is the oldest surviving map of the Holy Land.

megiddo.title: Megiddo
megiddo.note: It guarded the pass into the Jezreel Valley. A Canaanite royal city, it went to Manasseh and Solomon rebuilt it as a chariot city. Deborah and Barak beat Sisera on its plain, and King Josiah died there facing Pharaoh Necho, a death mourned so deeply it became proverbial. Thutmose III's siege of it around 1457 BC is carved in detail on the walls of Karnak.

mephaath.title: Mephaath
mephaath.note: A Levitical city in Reuben's land, given to the Merarite Levites. By Jeremiah's time Moab held it, so it turns up in his oracle against Moab. The site east of the Jordan has not been pinned down.

merom.title: Merom
merom.note: The waters where Joshua broke the northern Canaanite alliance under Jabin, king of Hazor. They are likely the marshy lake north of the Sea of Galilee now called Lake Huleh.

michmethath.title: Michmethath
michmethath.note: A landmark on the line between Ephraim and Manasseh, near Shechem. Joshua uses it only to mark the border, and no one has found the site.

middin.title: Middin
middin.note: "Measures." One of the six towns in the wilderness west of the Dead Sea, listed with En-gedi.

midian.title: Midian
midian.note: A people descended from Abraham through Keturah, and they keep turning up in different roles. Midianite traders bought Joseph. Moses found a home and a wife, Zipporah, in Midian. Later they oppressed Israel until Gideon beat them.

migdal-el.title: Migdal-el
migdal-el.note: "Tower of God," a fortified town of Naphtali. Some scholars have tied it to Magdala, Mary Magdalene's town, but the link is not certain.

migdal-gad.title: Migdal-gad
migdal-gad.note: In the lowland district of Judah, the Shephelah. The name means "tower of Gad," and it is generally placed at el-Mejdel near Ashkelon, which still keeps the word migdal.

milcah-2.title: Milcah
milcah-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
milcah-2.note: A different woman from Nahor's wife. This Milcah is one of the five sisters in Numbers 27 who asked for their father's land.

mishal.title: Mishal
mishal.note: A coastal town of Asher, probably near Mount Carmel, given with its pastures to the Gershonite Levites.

misrephoth-mayim.title: Misrephoth-mayim
misrephoth-mayim.note: Joshua chased the beaten northern Canaanites from the Waters of Merom as far as this place, and later it is listed as land still not taken in his old age. The name is usually read "burnings of water," maybe hot springs or lime kilns by the coast. It is generally put near the Mediterranean north of Acco, without much confidence.

mizpeh.title: Mizpeh
mizpeh.note: Another spelling of Mizpah, the watchpost name given to several places in Israel.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moladah.title: Moladah
moladah.note: In the Negev. Judah was given it first, then Simeon, whose land sat inside Judah's, and people moved back there after the exile. It is often placed at Tel Malhata, east of Beersheba.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

mozah.title: Mozah
mozah.note: A town of Benjamin, usually placed at Tel Moza just west of Jerusalem. Digging there has found a large Iron Age temple and a grain store.

naamah-3.title: Naamah
naamah-3.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

nahalal.title: Nahalal
nahalal.note: A town in Zebulun, later given with its pastures to the Merarite Levites. Zebulun never drove out the Canaanites there and put them to forced labour instead. It is sometimes linked with Tell en-Nahl near the Kishon River.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

neah.title: Neah
neah.note: On the border of Zebulun, not far from Rimmon. The site has not been firmly found.

neiel.title: Neiel
neiel.note: On Asher's southern border. It is tentatively placed at a ruin near where the Wadi esh-Shaghur comes out, north of Kabul in western Galilee.

neptoah.title: Neptoah
neptoah.note: The waters of Neptoah are a point on the border between Judah and Benjamin, named twice in Joshua. They are commonly linked to the spring at Lifta, just northwest of Jerusalem.

nezib.title: Nezib
nezib.note: In Judah's Shephelah, at the ruin of Khirbet Beit Nasib southwest of Hebron.

nibshan.title: Nibshan
nibshan.note: Six towns stood in Judah's wilderness by the western shore of the Dead Sea, and Nibshan was one. It is often put near En-gedi, without a firm site.

noah-2.title: Noah
noah-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
noah-2.note: Not the man of the flood. This Noah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who went to Moses and won the right to inherit their father's land, since there was no son.

non.title: Non
non.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
non.note: Joshua's father, of the tribe of Ephraim, more usually spelled Nun and hardly ever seen outside the phrase "Joshua son of Nun."

og.title: Og
og.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
og.note: King of Bashan and, in Deuteronomy, the last of the Rephaim, with a bed over thirteen feet long. Israel beat him and took his whole kingdom.

ophni.title: Ophni
ophni.note: A town given to Benjamin, listed in Joshua 18:24 with Geba and other places north of Jerusalem. Its site is uncertain.

ophrah-2.title: Ophrah
ophrah-2.note: Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.

othniel.title: Othniel
othniel.note: Caleb's younger relative, who won Caleb's daughter Achsah by taking a Canaanite city. He became Israel's first judge and broke eight years of oppression under a Mesopotamian king.

parah.title: Parah
parah.note: It means heifer. A town in Benjamin's lot, commonly placed at the ruins of Ain Fara, about six miles northeast of Jerusalem.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

pisgah.title: Pisgah
pisgah.note: Moses looked out over the promised land from the top of Pisgah before he died. Balak had brought Balaam up the same ridge in Moab to curse Israel's camp. It belongs to the range called Abarim.

rabbah.title: Rabbah
rabbah.note: Capital of Ammon. David's army besieged it, and Uriah died in that siege, put where the fighting was worst on David's orders.

rabbith.title: Rabbith
rabbith.note: A border town of Issachar, named once in Joshua 19:20, and nobody knows its site.

rakkath.title: Rakkath
rakkath.note: Naphtali's fortified town on the shore of the Sea of Galilee. Jewish tradition says Herod Antipas later built Tiberias on top of it.

rakkon.title: Rakkon
rakkon.note: On the coast north of Joppa, near the mouth of the Yarkon, this town belonged to Dan. It is generally placed at Tell er-Reqqeit.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

ramah-2.title: Ramah
ramah-2.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

ramah-3.title: Ramah
ramah-3.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

ramoth.title: Ramoth
ramoth.note: Ramoth in Gilead, one of the cities of refuge east of the Jordan. Israel and Aram fought over it again and again. Ahab took his death wound there in disguise, and later Jehu was anointed king in the same place.

reba.title: Reba
reba.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
reba.note: One of five Midianite kings killed in the war Moses ordered shortly before his death. His land was later counted in Reuben's share. Joshua 13:21 lists him again with the others.

rehob.title: Rehob
rehob.note: The far edge of the spies' route into Canaan, up in the north. Asher was allotted a Rehob too, and Judges 1:31 says Asher never drove out the people living there.

rehob-3.title: Rehob
rehob-3.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

rekem-3.title: Rekem
rekem-3.note: Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

rekem.title: Rekem
rekem.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
rekem.note: One of the five Midianite kings Israel killed in the days of Moses. The same name belongs to a man in Manasseh's genealogy.

remeth-2.title: Remeth
remeth-2.note: A town of Issachar in Joshua's allotment list. It is probably the town listed elsewhere as Ramoth and Jarmuth.

remmon-4.title: Remmon
remmon-4.note: Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

remmon-3.title: Remmon
remmon-3.note: A town in the far south, named in the town lists of Joshua 15:32 and 19:7 and again in 1 Chronicles 4:32.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

rumah-2.title: Rumah
rumah-2.note: A town in the hill-country list of Judah (Joshua 15:52), and its site is uncertain.

salcah.title: Salcah
salcah.note: The eastern edge of Israelite settlement. Salcah was a city of Bashan, given to the half tribe of Manasseh once Og, king of Bashan, was beaten.

sansannah.title: Sansannah
sansannah.note: A town in the Negev of Judah. Joshua 19:5 calls it Hazar-susah and 1 Chronicles 4:31 calls it Hazar-susim, and the names mean roughly village of the horse.

sarid.title: Sarid
sarid.note: On Zebulun's border, west of Chisloth-tabor. Nobody has pinned down the site, though several ruins in the eastern Jezreel valley have been put forward.

secacah.title: Secacah
secacah.note: In Judah's wilderness district on the western shore of the Dead Sea, one of six towns listed with Beth-arabah, Middin and En-gedi. Its exact site is unknown.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

shaalabbin.title: Shaalabbin
shaalabbin.note: Allotted to Dan, but the Danites never fully took it, and Amorites held on there until they were put to forced labour. It is also spelled Shaalbim.

shaaraim.title: Shaaraim
shaaraim.note: The name means two gates. When David killed Goliath, the Philistines fled along the road past this Shaaraim, out in the Shephelah.

shahazimah.title: Shahazimah
shahazimah.note: A border town of Issachar. The name means toward the heights, and nobody knows where it was.

shamir-3.title: Shamir
shamir-3.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

sharuhen-2.title: Sharuhen
sharuhen-2.note: A town of Simeon inside Judah's land, called Shaaraim in 1 Chronicles 4:31. Egyptian records describe a fortress by this name that the Hyksos held.

sheba-2.title: Sheba
sheba-2.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
sheba-2.note: He raised a revolt against David in 2 Samuel 20 and called the northern tribes away from him. It ended at a walled town, with his head thrown over the wall to the men outside.

shebam.title: Shebam
shebam.note: Good grazing land east of the Jordan, taken from Sihon, which Reuben and Gad asked for because of their flocks.

shechem.title: Shechem
shechem.note: Abram stopped here when he first came into the land, and Joseph's brothers were grazing the flocks near it when Joseph went looking for them. The city took its name from a Canaanite prince.

shechem-3.title: Shechem
shechem-3.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shechem-3.note: A different Shechem from the prince, named in the clan lists at Numbers 26:31 and Joshua 17:2.

shema-4.title: Shema
shema-4.note: A town of Judah in the Negev, among the southernmost cities near the border of Edom. It is generally identified with the Sheba of Joshua 19:2.

shemida.title: Shemida
shemida.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shemida.note: Gilead's son and Manasseh's great-grandson, and his descendants made one of the clans of Manasseh.

sheshai.title: Sheshai
sheshai.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sheshai.note: One of the sons of Anak. Caleb drove him out of Hebron when he finally claimed the land promised to him decades earlier.

shicron.title: Shicron
shicron.note: A landmark on Judah's northern border, between Ekron and Jabneel near the coast. Nothing else is recorded of it, and the site is unknown.

shihon.title: Shihon
shihon.note: A town of Issachar, named only in Joshua 19:19, and still not found.

shihor.title: Shihor
shihor.note: The stream on Egypt's northeastern border. It marks the southwestern edge of the land promised to Israel.

shihor-libnath.title: Shihor-libnath
shihor-libnath.note: Not a person but a stream on the southern boundary of Asher. It is generally identified with the Nahr Zarqa, which rises in the Carmel range.

shilhim.title: Shilhim
shilhim.note: A town in the south of Judah, near the border with Simeon. It is generally identified with the Sharuhen of Joshua 19:6, which Egyptian sources know as a fortress.

shiloh.title: Shiloh
shiloh.note: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, north of Bethel in Ephraim, for most of the time of the judges. Young Samuel served there. After the Philistines captured the ark, the place faded.

shimon-meron.title: Shimon-meron
shimon-meron.note: Joshua beat thirty-one kings west of the Jordan, and the king of Shimon-meron was one of them. It is generally taken to be the same place as Shimron.

shimron-2.title: Shimron
shimron-2.note: Named twice, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

shocho.title: Shocho
shocho.note: A town of Judah near the Valley of Elah, close to where David fought Goliath.

shocho-3.title: Shocho
shocho-3.note: Named once, in Joshua, and nowhere else.

shunem.title: Shunem
shunem.note: A village of Issachar near Jezreel. The Philistines camped here before the battle on Mount Gilboa where Saul and his sons died, and a woman here built a room for Elisha.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

succoth.title: Succoth
succoth.note: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.

taanach.title: Taanach
taanach.note: A Canaanite royal city on the southwest edge of the Jezreel Valley, near Megiddo. Joshua beat its king, the town went to the Levites of Kohath, and its Canaanites were never driven out. Deborah's song puts a battle there by the waters of Megiddo.

taanath-shiloh.title: Taanath-shiloh
taanath-shiloh.note: A point on Ephraim's southern border, named once in Joshua 16:6. The name seems to mean approach to Shiloh, and it is commonly identified with the ruin of Ta'na southeast of Shechem.

tabor.title: Tabor
tabor.note: A dome-shaped mountain rising out of the Jezreel Valley, on the line between Zebulun and Issachar. Deborah sent Barak there to gather Israel before the battle with Sisera. The psalmist sets it beside Hermon, and Hosea and Jeremiah both name it in oracles of judgment.

talmai-2.title: Talmai
